title: Republics of the Soviet Union
capsule: The constituent republics of the Soviet Union were the fifteen union republics (Soviet Socialist Republics) that formally composed the USSR from its founding treaty of December 1922 until dissolution in December 1991, each nominally sovereign but in practice subject to the Communist Party of the Soviet Union. The dataset's narrow 1920–1921 span captures the transitional moment when the Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic and several proto-SSRs existed before the formal 1922 Union treaty, as Bolshevik forces consolidated control over the former Russian Empire's borderlands including Ukraine, Byelorussia, and the Transcaucasian republics. The entity as a collective political-administrative category persisted until the August 1991 coup attempt accelerated declarations of independence, with Gorbachev dissolving the USSR on 25 December 1991.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Soviet administrative boundaries are among the most precisely documented in the dataset, defined by official decrees and census records; the 1920–1921 pre-union transitional boundaries are less sharply defined than post-1922 SSR borders.
